subject: ramenStall
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: night ramen stall with lanterns and stools.
Style: Studio Ghibli.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Studio Ghibli-style night ramen stall diorama as a single TypeScript module using the agentic-3js-builder SDK, targeting a static scene of roughly 180-340 parts with textures and lantern glows. I'm sketching out the yatai cart structure—wooden counter, canopy roof, and noren curtains—as the core elements of the build.

Since this is a static scenery piece, I'm skipping joints entirely and keeping all geometry in model space under the root group, which simplifies things considerably. I'm listing out what's needed: a noren curtain with ramen kanji, paper lanterns with text, a menu board, steam effects, wood grain paint for the cart, mottled cloth for the canopy, and copper-toned metal paint for the pot, plus maybe a small cat for Ghibli charm.

Now I'm working out the actual coordinates for the yatai cart: the base body box sized around 2.0 x 0.78 x 0.7 with wood-grain panels, a counter slab on top, two wheels with spoke details positioned at the back corners, and four vertical corner posts to support a canopy frame.

I'm then designing the roof as a pitched canopy with angled slabs and a ridge beam over the posts, finished in dark indigo canvas with trim, plus a split three-panel noren curtain hanging from the front eave.

For the noren itself, I'm using double-sided hanging cards with a lean of 180 degrees so they drape downward, textured with an SVG showing dark indigo fabric and white kanji — accounting for the fact that the card's orientation means the drawing needs to be flipped since it reads upside down when hung this way.

For the lanterns, I'm shaping them as scaled sphere geometry to get that bulbous chochin silhouette, wrapped in a texture with a red background, dark rib lines, and kanji text, since painted surfaces alone can't capture the glow effect I want.

Now I'm planning the placement: two lanterns hanging from the front eave corners around x=±1.05, and a larger one hanging from a side bracket, plus small black top/bottom caps and a hanging wire for realism. I'll also add round stools out front near the entrance.

Then I'm detailing the counter setup—bowls with a lathe-painted blue rim, chopsticks, a copper-toned pot steaming over the stove at the back-left, a kettle, stacked bowls, a hanging menu board, a sake bottle, and condiment jars, with a box-shaped stove base beneath the pot.

I'm placing the pot at a recessed stove position toward the back-left, adding a hanging paper sign reading "営業中", and considering a small Ghibli-style cat (body, head, ears, tail, glowing eyes) sitting on the far-right stool as a static decorative element rather than a jointed creature.

For scenery, I'll add a thin cobblestone base disc about 0.04m thick under the whole stall and stools, since the diorama format implies a ground surface even though the brief doesn't explicitly name one.

For lighting, I'm planning warm glow effects: lanterns, a fire glow in the stove pot, a hanging bulb under the roof, and maybe a subtle glow on the steam.

I'm sketching out the code imports and helper functions I'll need — builder utilities, glow and metal kits, plus wrapper functions for boxes and cylinders to keep the structure clean.

Now I'm defining the color palette for a nighttime scene: a textured wood tone darkened toward the shadows, plus indigo, cream, red, lantern orange, black, and brass via the metal kit.

For the roof, I'm building a pitched canopy using two tilted boxes forming a peak, working out the trigonometry so the front and back edges slope down symmetrically from the ridge line.

I'll paint the roof panels with mottled indigo tones and add a cream trim stripe along the eaves based on z-position, plus a ridge beam cylinder for detail. For a Ghibli-style touch, I'm considering adding a scalloped trim strip along the front eave with half-circle bumps extruded along its length.

Now I'm placing structural posts running from the counter up to the roof underside, positioned front and back, calculating their heights to match the roof's slope angle, and adding cross beams connecting them. Then I'll hang a noren curtain beneath the front beam.

For the noren, I'm dividing it into three indigo panels with small gaps between them, each displaying white kanji for "らーめん" split across the panels.

For lanterns, I'm writing a texture function that draws a red background with horizontal ribs and kanji centered at the front-facing part, since the sphere wrap means only the middle portion of the drawing shows through the front.

For the stools, I'm sketching red lacquer seats with splayed legs and a connecting brace ring, trying to figure out how to sweep a closed circular path for that ring geometry.

Now I'm working out the bowl shape by defining a lathe profile that traces foot, outer wall, rim, and inner wall points carefully so the cross-section doesn't self-intersect.

For coloring, I'm thinking through how to distinguish the rim, broth interior, and porcelain surfaces using height and normal direction, then planning to add curled noodle sweeps and a narutomaki slice inside the bowl.

Now I'm sketching the pot setup with a copper cylinder, a brass lathe-dome lid with knob, and a few semi-transparent steam card sprites rising from the top, plus a stove box beneath.

I'm also planning a hanging menu board on a post with cream background and brown Japanese text for ramen, gyoza, and beer prices, strung up near the counter's left front post.

For the roof and surroundings, I'm adding a glowing bulb under the ridge with a cord and tin shade, plus side details like a water bucket, a red "open" sign plate hanging from the eave, and a back shelf with sake bottles. For the cat, I'm placing it sitting on one of the stools near the counter.

Now I'm shaping the cat itself: a capsule body, rounded head with spiky ears, a curling tail, small front paws, and glowing yellow eyes with dark vertical pupils, all in black fur with a cream chest patch, facing toward the viewer.

For the ground, I'm making a flat stone-textured cylinder base with cobblestone paint patches on top and dark grout edges, then roughly tallying up all the diorama's parts—cart, wheels, posts, roof, lanterns, stools, bowls, pot, stove—to plan the full scene's complexity.

I'm adding a few more details like a kettle, towel, crate, and condiment jars, then setting up the builder and defining wood grain paint textures for the materials.
